newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end down on speculative selling.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end down on speculative selling.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended marginally lower on Thursday, dragged down by speculative selling in Huangshan Tourism Development 900942.SS ahead of the close, brokers said.
The B index edged down 0.028 point or 0.04 percent to 72.903 on volume of 10.321 million worth $3.931 million compared with $4.330 million on Wednesday.
Trading was light with many foreign investors turning their attention to the soaring Hong Kong stock market. The index was seen consolidating around the 73-point level over the near term.
"As major investors were sidelined, trading was very sluggish despite some bargain-hunting," said one broker.

There was little market response to news that economic tsar Zhu Rongji urged lumbering state firms to look to the stock market as a means to raise capital rather than relying on bank credits, brokers said.
"The positive news failed to activate the B share market, as major investors are trading in Hong Kong," one broker said.
Despite the fall in the index, gainers outpaced losers. Of the 45 B share issues, 42 were traded, with 21 rising and 16 down. Five were unchanged.
Shanghai Huili Building Materials was the biggest loser on expectations of disappointing interim results. It shed $0.020 or 9.52 percent to $0.190 on volume of 332,000 shares.
Shanghai Refrigerator Compressor was the most active issue, rebounding from recent losses. It gained $0.010 or 2.57 percent to $0.398 on volume of 921,300 shares.
Shanghai's A share index extended its upward climb on active buying of companies that have listings in Hong Kong where the market is at record levels, brokers said.
The index rose 11.122 points or 0.90 percent to 1,245.578 as 353.9 million shares worth 3.6 billion yuan were traded. The SSE30 blue chip index rose 50.127 points or 1.35 percent to 3,761.326.
Yizheng Chemical Fibre surged 0.28 yuan or 5.97 percent to 4.97.
Brokers linked the rise to a possible restructuring or merger but a company official said there was no such plan. Yizheng's Hong Kong shares were suspended pending an announcement.
Shanghai Steel Tube Co was aided by speculative buying late in the session. It surged 0.57 yuan or 10.00 percent to 6.27 yuan on volume of 287,700 shares.

Brokers also said there was renewed talk of a cut in commercial bank reserve requirements but a central bank official told Reuters there was no such plan at the moment. --Shanghai Newsroom (86-21) 6279-7004
